name: Content Provenance and Synthetic-Media Labelling
question: Can people tell that an image, video or voice was made by AI?
summary: Generative tools that produce realistic images, video or voice increasingly have to mark their output. Three layers work together: a visible label or audio disclosure people notice, signed provenance metadata such as C2PA Content Credentials that records how the file was made, and an invisible watermark that can survive screenshots and re-encoding when metadata is stripped. In India, the IT Amendment Rules 2026 (notified 16 February, in force 20 February 2026) require intermediaries offering tools that create synthetically generated audio-visual content to label it prominently, embed permanent metadata or an identifier where feasible and not allow labels or metadata to be removed, with extra user-declaration duties for significant social media intermediaries. The EU AI Act adds transparency duties for synthetic content and deepfakes from August 2026. This is an educational summary, not legal advice; confirm scope and details with counsel.
useCases: Tools that generate realistic images, video, voice or avatars
Marketing and media teams publishing AI-made assets
Platforms that host user uploads and must detect and label synthetic media

steps.title: Know what is in scope
steps.text: Rangmanch Studio, a fictional ad-tech company, makes realistic product images, avatar videos and Hindi voice ads. These are synthetic audio-visual content; its text captions are treated separately.

steps.title: Add a visible label
steps.text: Every image gets a clear “AI-generated · AI द्वारा निर्मित” band, and every voice ad starts with a spoken disclosure. The label is on by default.

steps.title: Sign provenance metadata
steps.text: A C2PA manifest records that the asset was created by a trained algorithm, by which tool and when, signed with the company’s certificate.

steps.title: Add an invisible watermark
steps.text: A watermark tied to the asset id survives screenshots and re-encoding that strip metadata. The watermark call stands for whichever watermarking SDK is used.

steps.title: Lock it in the tool
steps.text: The export dialog has no option to remove the label or credentials, as the Indian rules expect of tools that create such content.

steps.title: Test the real sharing path
steps.text: Each week 50 assets are shared through messaging and social apps. Labels survive 70% of the time, C2PA metadata rarely does, and with the watermark about 96% stay identifiable.

practice.scenario: Rangmanch Studio, a fictional ad-tech company, generates product images, avatar videos and Hindi voice ads for Indian brands. After India’s IT Amendment Rules 2026 came into force on 20 February 2026, it labels every visual asset with “AI-generated · AI द्वारा निर्मित”, starts every voice ad with a spoken disclosure, signs C2PA Content Credentials, adds an invisible watermark tied to the asset id, and removes the option to strip them at export. In weekly tests through messaging and social apps, about 96% of assets stay identifiable as AI-made, against 70% with labels and metadata alone. This is an educational example, not legal advice.

practice.analogy: A hallmark on gold jewellery: a visible stamp anyone can read, a certificate that travels with it, and a mark in the metal itself that an assayer can find even if the certificate is lost.

library.name: c2patool
library.what: The Content Authenticity Initiative’s command-line tool adds and reads C2PA manifests on images, video and audio.
library.install: cargo install c2patool  (or download a release binary)

practice.note: Without signing settings c2patool uses a test certificate; production signing needs your own certificate. Checking survival means re-downloading assets after sharing them through the real apps.

numericDrill.question: Visible labels plus metadata survive sharing on 70% of assets. An invisible watermark survives on 85% of the rest. What share stays identifiable overall, in percent?
numericDrill.answer: Missing after labels: 30%. The watermark recovers 85% of those: 0.3 × 0.85 = 25.5%. Total 70 + 25.5 = 95.5%.

interview.question: How would you mark AI-generated images and audio?
interview.answer: Add a visible label or spoken disclosure by default, sign C2PA Content Credentials, add an invisible watermark tied to an asset id, stop users removing them, and test survival through real sharing paths.

interview.question: What do India’s 2026 IT Rules amendments require of generative tools?
interview.answer: In summary: intermediaries offering tools that create realistic synthetic audio-visual content must label it prominently, embed permanent metadata or an identifier where feasible, and not allow removal; significant social media intermediaries must also collect user declarations and verify them. Confirm details with counsel.
